chapter: Ecological Adaptations, Succession and Ecological Services
question_text: Name the type of land plants that can tolerate the salinities of the sea.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 13, book p.35, VSAQ 4. The book prints 'Halophytes. Ex: Rhizophora'; the definition line and the pneumatophore point are added from standard ecology. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The 1+1 split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Ecological Adaptations, Succession and Ecological Services · 2 marks

steps.label: The name
lines: Halophytes are plants that grow in soil
with a high salt content — sea coasts,
steps.why: Halo means salt and phyte means plant, so the name itself states the habitat the question describes.
common_mistakes: Writing hydrophytes. Hydrophytes grow in fresh water and cannot tolerate sea salt.
Writing mangroves as the type name. Mangrove is the forest; halophyte is the plant type.
steps.memory_tip: Halo = salt, as in halogen and halite. Halophyte = salt plant.
steps.margin_note: The word halophyte alone earns the first mark. Add the habitat line.

steps.label: Example and feature
lines: Their roots grow in salty mud that has little
air, so special roots called pneumatophores
(breathing roots) grow upward out of the
mud and carry out gas exchange.
steps.why: The example is what an examiner checks first. Rhizophora is the standard one, and its pneumatophores show how a halophyte handles a waterlogged salty soil.
common_mistakes: Giving no example at all. This chapter marks the example separately.
Calling pneumatophores prop roots. Prop roots hang down; pneumatophores grow up.
steps.memory_tip: Pneuma means air. Pneumatophore = the root that reaches air.
steps.margin_note: One example is enough. The pneumatophore line is the safe extra.

insider_note: Almost every student writes halophytes and stops. The second mark is usually the example, so always write Rhizophora.
